# Eleven green end-to-end runs while checkout was broken in every one of them

## Problem Description

Larder is our React Native grocery app. Build 412 went out on Tuesday and
support had 40 tickets by Thursday morning: you tap **Place order**, the order
is created, and then the app sits on a blank white screen forever. The
confirmation screen throws on render because the orders API renamed
`order.reference` to `order.referenceCode` back in build 401 and nobody updated
the screen. That part is understood and a fix is already in review — I am not
asking about the app bug, and I do not want anyone touching
`app/OrderConfirmationScreen.jsx`.

What I have to explain to my director on Monday is the CI history. The
end-to-end job on `main` ran eleven times between build 401 and build 412 and
was green all eleven times. `e2e/checkout.test.js` taps through the basket,
places an order, and checks the confirmation screen and the reference printed
on it. The confirmation screen has not rendered since the second of July.

Two people have opinions and I have to answer both of them by Monday:

- Priya wants `testTimeout` in the Jest config raised from two minutes to five.
  Her theory is that the CI simulators are slower than our laptops and things
  are being cut off before they finish.
- Marcus wrote a `settle()` helper — three seconds of waiting after a tap — and
  merged it into `e2e/account.test.js` three weeks ago. That file has needed
  nothing since, which is more than anyone else can say, and he wants it across
  the other 11 spec files before 1.9.0. Nobody has offered an alternative and I
  am fairly close to letting him do it.

Four spec files are attached, along with the run history, the Jest config, the
confirmation screen and the promo banner component. Tell me why the job did not
go red on any of the eleven builds, and give me back specs I can trust.

## Output Specification

1. Go through the four attached spec files and repair any that would not have
   gone red on build 412. Leave alone any that are already sound, and do not
   change which behaviours a spec checks or delete a spec.
2. Write `docs/why-eleven-runs-were-green.md` explaining the CI history, and
   give me your answer on Marcus's helper and on Priya's timeout so I can put it
   in writing on Monday.
3. Say in that document what the remaining 8 spec files need from us.
evals.expected_output:
1. Go through the four attached spec files and repair any that would not have
   gone red on build 412. Leave alone any that are already sound, and do not
   change which behaviours a spec checks or delete a spec.
2. Write `docs/why-eleven-runs-were-green.md` explaining the CI history, and
   give me your answer on Marcus's helper and on Priya's timeout so I can put it
   in writing on Monday.
3. Say in that document what the remaining 8 spec files need from us.
assertions: docs/why-eleven-runs-were-green.md exists, answers Marcus and Priya separately, and says what the remaining 8 spec files need. A document that addresses only one of the two people scores at most half.

The document states that the wait chains in e2e/checkout.test.js are unterminated, so awaiting them resolves immediately on an object that never ran the wait and never checked anything — the spec could not fail whatever the app did. Attributing the eleven green runs to slow simulators, to intermittency, to the app bug being caught elsewhere, or to a missing assertion library scores zero. Saying the waits 'are missing a timeout' without stating that the assertion therefore never ran, so the file was incapable of reporting a failure, scores at most half. Citing the 0.9s duration against the four-second manual timing is not required for full marks but a document that reaches the conclusion with no evidence from the run history scores at most half.

`does not show an error for a valid promo code` asserts against `promo-error`, which no component renders — app/PromoBanner.jsx renders `promo-error-banner` — so the check passes because the element is absent rather than because the app is correct. Full marks require repairing the spec to name the identifier that exists (or otherwise making the check able to fail) AND saying in the document that an absence assertion against a non-existent identifier is always green. Leaving promos.test.js untouched scores zero. Editing it without noticing the identifier mismatch — for example only adding a wait — scores zero.

MUST NOT endorse rolling `settle()` across the other spec files, and MUST NOT leave the existing calls in e2e/account.test.js in place: fixed sleeps between actions mask real synchronisation problems rather than fix them. Approving the rollout, or approving it 'as a temporary measure until the specs are repaired', scores zero. Removing the calls from account.test.js but giving no verdict on the rollout scores at most half.

After the sleeps come out, `uploads an avatar` must still tolerate the 9.4-13.8s CDN upload the report measures — an explicit bounded wait on the avatar image with a timeout comfortably above that range. Deleting the three sleeps and leaving the bare assertion scores zero: the default assertion timeout is far shorter than the measured upload and the spec that was passing now fails. Substituting a different fixed sleep scores zero. Choosing a timeout at or under the measured range scores at most half.

MUST NOT change `testTimeout` in e2e/jest.config.js. Nothing in the job has ever approached the two-minute limit — the whole suite finishes in 44 seconds — so the change addresses a failure mode that is not occurring. Landing the config change scores zero. Declining it without saying why it cannot be the cause scores at most half.

MUST NOT modify e2e/search.test.js, which uses plain auto-waiting assertions and would have gone red on build 412 already, and MUST NOT modify app/OrderConfirmationScreen.jsx, which the request rules out. Any edit to either scores zero here.

# A reinstall before every spec fixed the order-dependence and tripled the CI bill

## Problem Description

Larder is our React Native grocery app. It has ten end-to-end spec files. Run
any one of them alone and it is green. Run the whole suite and everything from
the third file onwards falls over with `element(by.id('home-search')) not
found`, because the file before it finished on the order-detail screen and the
next one starts by assuming it is on home. Our fault, nobody else's.

A contractor fixed it on 29 August by putting a full uninstall and reinstall of
the app into the shared `beforeEach`, so every spec starts from a virgin
install. It worked. It also took the suite from **4m12s to 44m56s** and our
macOS runner minutes for September are 2.9x August. Finance found it before we
did. His contract ended on Friday.

Priya has PR #764 open and it is the only proposal anyone has actually written.
It drops the reinstall and starts a fresh copy of the already-installed app
before each spec instead, with a 1.5 second settle afterwards because the first
tap on a cold process was landing before the bundle was ready. Nine consecutive
green nights, **9m50s**, three approvals. Her note on the patch argues the
point directly: a JS-level reload only swaps the bundle, so anything the native
side is still holding — the navigation stack, the image cache, the keyboard —
survives it, and a fresh process is the only reset she trusts, for six seconds
a spec. I am one click from merging it and I would like to know if I should.

The other thing I want out of this is one rule that covers every spec file.
Three of the ten currently do their own thing in their own hooks, and Marek is
right that ten different answers to "how does a spec start" is exactly the mess
I am trying to leave — every exception is one more thing the next person has to
learn before they can write a spec. He wants the hold-outs brought into line
with whatever the shared rule ends up being. Priya deliberately left them alone
because she did not want to touch anything she did not understand.

The shared hooks, five of the ten spec files, Priya's patch, the timings and
the onboarding module with its unit tests are attached.

## Output Specification

1. Decide what PR #764 should become and land that: rewrite `e2e/init.js`, and
   edit any spec file your decision actually changes.
2. Write `docs/e2e-lifecycle.md` — the rule for how a spec starts, the answer
   Priya gets on her patch, and the answer Marek gets on the hold-outs.
3. State in that document what you expect the suite to cost once your change is
   in, and on what basis.

1. Decide what PR #764 should become and land that: rewrite `e2e/init.js`, and

2. Write `docs/e2e-lifecycle.md` — the rule for how a spec starts, the answer
   Priya gets on her patch, and the answer Marek gets on the hold-outs.
3. State in that document what you expect the suite to cost once your change is
   in, and on what basis.
assertions: The shared per-spec hook in e2e/init.js MUST NOT call device.launchApp(...) in any form - not {delete: true}, not {newInstance: true}, not a bare relaunch. Keeping Priya's relaunch, or merging PR #764 with only the settle removed, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require device.reloadReactNative() as the shared per-spec reset with at most a single launch at suite start, plus the rebuttal to Priya's argument grounded in the evidence: every one of the 14 original failures was a spec's first line naming a screen the previous file navigated away from, and none was stale cart, filter, session or tour state, so what leaked was in-memory JS state and nothing native. Switching to the reload without engaging her argument at all scores at most half.

Deleting that hook, or downgrading it to the shared reload or to a relaunch, scores zero - app/onboarding-gate.js reads the tour flag out of persistent device storage, so a bundle reload leaves it set and the first spec can only pass once per install. Keeping the hook but never saying why - i.e. leaving it as an unexplained special case the next person still has to learn - scores at most half.

# The whole mobile suite froze the day pull-to-refresh landed, and the app is frozen too

## Problem Description

Larder (React Native, iOS + Android) had a fourteen-spec end-to-end suite that
ran in about four minutes and had been boring for a year. Sprint 44 merged two
things on the same afternoon:

- a pull-to-refresh spinner on the orders list, and
- a telemetry stream that keeps a long poll open to
  `https://telemetry.larder.internal/v1/telemetry/stream` for session analytics.

Since that merge **every one of the fourteen specs fails**, and they all fail
the same way: the first `tap()` in the spec never completes and two minutes
later the runner kills it. Not one spec reaches its assertions. Nobody touched
the specs — `git log e2e/` has no commits in six weeks. It reproduces on every
developer's machine and on both CI runners, iOS and Android alike, first try,
every time.

Here is my problem. The release branch was cut on Tuesday and the app source is
frozen until Thursday's build ships. The release manager is taking crash fixes
and nothing else, and he is certainly not taking a change to a loading spinner
because a test runner is unhappy with it. So whatever we do this week has to
live in the test layer.

Which is exactly what Aleks has done. PR #812 is open, the suite is green in
three minutes and eight seconds with it, three people have approved it, and
code freeze is Friday. He is not being lazy, he is being pragmatic — a red
suite blocks the release train and nobody else has produced anything at all. I
am the one who has to press the button and I would rather press it than explain
to the release manager why we slipped. Talk me out of it, or tell me to merge
it.

Separately: Ines has had a branch open since June with one spec for the live
tracking map. It has never passed. It fails the same way the fourteen do now,
except it was doing it three months before sprint 44, and it is the only spec
that ever did. We left it on the branch and forgot about it. Her spec, the
screen it drives and the vendor notes for the map package are attached with
everything else, and I would like an answer on that too while we are here.

The timeout logs, the new app code, the current global setup, one
representative spec and Aleks's patch are attached.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/rca-suite-freeze.md` — what is blocking the taps, what
   introduced it, your verdict on PR #812 with the reasoning behind it, and
   your answer on the freeze.
2. Make the edits your recommendation requires, wherever they belong.
3. Say what should happen to Ines's branch.
